meta: Where is a water softener installed? Usually on the main line after the shutoff, near a drain and outlet. Placement tips for Oakley, CA. Call (888) 910-8644.
lead: A water softener in Oakley, CA is normally installed on the main water line right after the shutoff, ahead of the water heater, close to a floor drain and a power outlet.
intro: A water softener is a tank-based system that swaps hardness minerals for sodium or potassium so scale stops building up in pipes and heaters. Most homes put it in the garage, a side yard enclosure or a utility closet where the supply line first enters the building.
This page explains why that spot works, how to compare the usual locations, what the installer needs within reach, and how local water numbers from Diablo Water District fit into the decision.

sections.h2: The logic behind the standard spot
paras: Softened water is only useful where it is needed, so the unit tees into the cold line downstream of the main shutoff. That placement lets you isolate the house and service the softener without draining anything else. Putting it ahead of the water heater matters because scale forms fastest when water is heated.

The system also has to dump brine and rinse water when it regenerates. That discharge needs a legal air gap into a drain, and the control head needs standard household power. Those two requirements shape where the equipment can realistically live.

sections.h2: Garage, side yard or closet: choosing a home for the tank
paras: Each location has trade-offs. The right one depends on where your main line enters and how far the nearest drain sits from it.

sections.h2: What the installer needs within reach

items.d: A few feet of accessible pipe for the inlet, outlet and bypass assembly. A cramped corner can force extra fittings.

items.t: A drain that meets the air gap
items.d: Regeneration water has to leave through a drain or standpipe, not a hose dropped in a bucket.
The timer or meter head runs on a small plug-in transformer, so an outlet within cord length saves an electrician visit.
A filled brine tank is heavy, and the resin tank must stand upright without rocking.
You will add salt regularly, so leave a clear arm's length on top.

sections.h2: Bypass valves and outdoor hose bibs
paras: A bypass valve lets water skip the softener during repairs or if the unit fails. Make sure everyone in the household knows where it is and which position means treated water. Ask the installer to label both positions with tape on the first day.

Outdoor faucets are another detail. Plumbing the softener before the outside lines means your lawn hose and car-wash bucket draw salty softened water, which wastes salt and capacity. A good layout feeds the hose bibs from the untreated side, so you only soften the water you actually bathe and wash with.
bullets: Keep a cold-water tap in the kitchen on the softened line only if you are comfortable with the added sodium
Ask whether a separate drinking-water filter makes more sense for taste
Choose a salt type recommended in the manual and keep the lid dry

sections.h2: Who handles what on installation day
paras: A plumber cuts into the main, sets the bypass, runs the drain and programs the head to match your water. For ordinary equipment installation we treat this under [[water-softener-filtration|water softener and filtration]] work, and the connection tie-ins fall into regular [[plumbing-installation|plumbing installation]]. Whether a permit applies is for City building staff to answer.

Before you buy a unit, get the actual hardness number for your address from the utility report, not a rule of thumb. An oversized system wastes salt and an undersized one runs out of capacity mid-week.

localnote.h2: Oakley water numbers and your softener choice
localnote.source_type: Diablo Water District 2025 Annual Water Quality Report
paras: Water in the District averages about 7 grains per gallon of hardness, so a softener has real work to do at any of the locations below. On the usual scale that sits at the low end of hard, so a softener is a comfort and appliance-life choice, not an emergency. The practical step is to size the unit using that grains figure and your household's water use.

The same report gives average sodium of 59 mg/L, with a range of 48 to 77 mg/L, before any softener adds its own. Anyone on a sodium-restricted diet should ask a doctor and consider keeping one drinking tap on untreated water. You can request the full report from the District at 87 Carol Lane or through its website.

faqs.q: Can a softener be installed outdoors?
a: Yes, in a covered, level enclosure that protects the control head from sun and rain. Outdoor installs also need a drain for regeneration water and a protected power source.

faqs.q: Does the softener go before or after the water heater?
a: Before it. The heater is the fastest place for scale to form, so soft water should reach it first. Only the hot and cold lines you want treated should come off the softened side.

faqs.q: How close does it need to be to a drain?
a: Close enough for a short, sloped drain line with an air gap. If the nearest drain is far, a condensate-style pump can lift the discharge, which adds cost and one more part to maintain.

faqs.q: Will I need to leave the garage free for salt deliveries?
a: You mainly need an arm's length of clear space to pour bags in. Many owners keep a small shelf nearby so bags stay off the wet floor.

faqs.q: Is a softener worth it with Oakley water?
a: The District's average hardness is moderate, so many households see mostly spotting and slower scale buildup. Ask a plumber to read your fixtures and water heater before deciding.

If you are shopping in the area, our [[plumber-brentwood-ca|Brentwood]] page covers a neighboring system with a different water supplier, and the [[service-area|service area]] list shows where we work.
Compare the grains figure on your own report with any manufacturer's capacity chart.
Walking the proposed spot with the installer before anything is bought is far easier than moving a finished installation.
